newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Strong outlook seen for Australia wine stocks.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Strong outlook seen for Australia wine stocks.

text.p: Australian wine makers had a sparkling financial year, with strong profits and surging share prices pushed by an excellent 1996 vintage and continuing talk of industry rationalisation, a trend expected to continue.
"We believe the wine sector will continue to outperform the All Ordinaries ... the immediate outlook for the industry is positive," stockbroker J.B Were & Son said in a research report.
Were pointed to sustainable earnings growth in the long term and continued speculation on corporate activity and rationalisation in the short term.
Strong sales in existing export markets, new market potential, and growing domestic demand for bottled wine were factors driving earnings growth, Were said.

Key sectoral trends in results for 1995/96 were strong revenue growth of 18 percent, compared to the non-bank industrial companies which reported 5.7 percent growth, and 37 percent growth in earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) for wine compared to 4.9 percent for the industrials, it said.
EBIT to sales margins improved almost three percentage points to 19.6 percent, against the non-bank industrials' slip of nearly one point to 8.7 percent.
This was due to improved asset use and premium price rises flowing from strong demand and short supply, Were said

The industry is dominated by four key players: Southcorp Wines, part of diversified manufacturer Southcorp Holdings Ltd, Mildara Blass, a unit of Foster's Brewing Group Ltd, France-based Pernod Ricard's Orlando Wyndham, and the only major pure wine play, BRL Hardy Ltd.
Behind them come a host of much smaller companies whose share prices have also been boosted through the year.
Among them are Simeon Wines Ltd and Australian Vintage Ltd.
Were issued buy recommendations for BRL, Southcorp, Petaluma and Simeon, and holds for Foster's, Peter Lehmann Wines Ltd and Brian McGuigan Wines Ltd.
However, Day Cutten analyst Roly Michelmore told Reuters he believed wine stocks were a little overvalued, with general enthusiasm driven by excellent export results and the 1996 vintage.
"The reason the prices are holding up there has as much to do with that now as takeover speculation," he said.
Michelmore said he believed the market got enthused about the wine industry "as much as anything because of its mystique".

"When I speak to institutional investors, I get the feeling they like the wine industry because they like wine and all the stuff that goes with it and it's not always about investment potential: certainly private small investors I think get carried away by that kind of sentiment," he said.

Michelmore said on a price earnings ratio basis, he would expect the wine industry to be on a discount to the industrial market because of the extra risk from its agricultural base, but it was attracting a premium on good growth prospects.
"But if you actually track the earnings out a couple of years I think they are looking a bit expensive," he said.
He saw BRL, Peter Lehmann and Petaluma as overvalued, while he had issued an accumulate on Simeon shares at A$2.55.
Another broker who did not want to be named said he believed wine stocks were approaching fair value, although there was still quite a bit of value in Simeon.
He ascribed improved prices to the recovery from the poor 1995 vintage, a generally positive share market, and perennial takeover speculation.
